title.narrative: Reducing health inequalities and improving vulnerable populations' right to health in El Salvador

description.narrative:
The long-term impact of this project is to contribute to the reduction of health inequalities and improving the right to health for vulnerable populations in El Salvador by promoting a holistic approach to tackling non-communicable diseases. Chronic Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs) are the leading cause of mortality and disability in the population over 30 years of age worldwide and their prevalence continues to increase, with long-term health implications. Every year, the Pan American Health Organization reports 5.5 million deaths due to NCDs in the Americas alone. Additionally, 15 million individuals between the ages of 30 and 69 die worldwide, which are considered "premature" deaths. Shockingly, over 85% of these deaths occur in low- and middle-income countries.
It is clear that the poorest populations bear the brunt of diseases due to their limited access to healthcare and quality food resulting from poverty. In addition to this, they also face challenges such as the lack of suitable spaces for physical activities and the absence of programs focused on the health of the elderly. However, these unjust and unequal conditions can be modified and prevented. This project aims to contribute to reducing such inequalities by strengthening and expanding the services of the Clinic for NCDs with a focus on the right to health. The public health system in El Salvador has structural weaknesses that fail to provide comprehensive care for vulnerable populations who cannot access private health services. The project will prioritise health promotion and education, work with patient groups, home visits, and counselling. It will also train staff to enhance their capacity in an integrated approach to NCDs.
